I cut the install down to one step: you run it and paste your API key into a small browser page. The tests pass, but I haven't run the full install end to end, so the browser page and the new terminal output haven't been seen live yet. The full test suite passes (181 tests), including 2 new tests for the key page. Nothing is committed yet.

**What changed**
- **No questions:** `memo install` no longer asks for a provider, a model, or whether to replace an existing key. It uses OpenRouter with the default model (`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`).
- **Key page in the browser:** if no key is saved, a clean page opens on your own machine only (`127.0.0.1`, protected by a one-time token).
  - You paste the key and click Connect.
  - It makes one real test call right away. A wrong key is rejected on the page and not saved, and a good key shows "Connected".
  - If the browser fails or times out, setup falls back to the old hidden terminal prompt.
- **Old keys are reused:** a key from `key.txt` or an environment variable is moved into the encrypted store automatically, with no prompt. The plain `key.txt` stays on disk, and you get one line saying how to delete it.
- **Cleaner output:** there is a short banner, aligned status lines, a 3-line privacy note instead of the long block, and a clear "Next: `memo init`" at the end.
- **Opt-in flags:** `--choose` brings back the provider/model menu, `--new-key` replaces a saved key, `--terminal-key` skips the browser, and `--privacy` prints the full privacy text.

The code is in [src/ui/keypage.js](src/ui/keypage.js) and [src/install.js](src/install.js), with a short README note in [README.md](README.md).

- Your git status shows 8 deleted files (`P1-v1.patch`, `memo_phase*.patch`, and others). I didn't delete them, so please check whether that was you.
- The `.specstory` changes are unrelated and untouched.

Run `node bin/memo.js install` once and tell me what the page and the terminal look like. Then I can polish the page further or commit.

I added `memo reset`. It wipes MEMO from this machine so you can test a fresh install. I haven't run it, because it would delete your real setup. The tests still pass (181).

It removes:
- the background task
- the Claude Code hooks
- the `memo` command and its PATH entry
- the saved API key
- the `~/.memo` folder (settings, logs)

It does not touch `.memory/` inside your repos. Run `memo clear --all-repo-data` if you want those gone too.

Test cycle:
```
memo reset
node bin/memo.js install
```
or double-click `setup_memo.bat`.

The command is registered in [bin/memo.js](bin/memo.js) and listed in `memo --help`. It reuses the existing `memo uninstall` logic, so there is no new deletion code.
